title: Graceful degradation for region-tied version pinning under capacity bursts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: When customers pin traffic to a specific model version in a region (region-tied pinning) and we run staged rollouts (canary / A-B), sudden capacity pressure or transient region degradation can cause either: 1) traffic to fail if pinned capacity is exhausted, or 2) unsafe automatic fallback to a different model variant without preserving customer pin semantics. Both outcomes violate SLO expectations and customer intent.

Goal: Design a deterministic, observable, and configurable graceful degradation policy that preserves model-version pinning semantics where possible, but allows bounded, auditable deviations under capacity or network partitions. The policy should interact cleanly with canary/A-B rollouts, honor sticky session affinity, and provide clear operator controls in Console and APIs.

Scope: Runtime routing resolver, rollout controller, Console controls (read-only telemetry + toggles), and SDK/REST error semantics. Not in scope: model compilation/quantization changes or long-lived data plane re-architecture.

Acceptance criteria:
- A routing policy spec that describes fallback precedence for region->tier->version pinning and canary cohorts.
- Implementation plan with rollback safe steps and a prototype in staging that demonstrates: (a) controlled fallback to configured compatible variant, (b) bounded-period sticky affinity retention, (c) audit logs that show when pin semantics were relaxed.
- Console UX mock showing a per-pin "degradation tolerance" and a timeline of fallback events.
- E2E tests covering burst scenarios, region partition, and canary vs pinned traffic mixes.

Design summary of proposed approach:
1) Two-tier pin contract: "Hard Pin" (must never route off-version unless explicit override) and "Soft Pin" (prefer pinned version but allow fallback under constrained conditions). Default for user-pinned versions is Soft Pin unless account-level restricts via policy.
2) Capacity-aware decision window: runtime maintains short-lived (10s-60s) token-buckets per (region, tier, version) to detect exhaustion. If depleted, the resolver consults fallback matrix rather than immediately failing.
3) Fallback matrix resolution order (configurable by customer): region-local compatible variants -> regional alternate tier (same region, lower performance tier) -> cross-region pinned-compatible variant -> last-resort: best-effort compatible model in best-effort tier.
4) Canary/A-B interactions: canary cohorts are tagged; routing resolver prefers preserving cohort assignment whenever fallback candidate belongs to same cohort set. If unavailable, fallback moves to the nearest cohort-preserving variant to avoid throwing canary metrics off.
5) Sticky affinity expiry: maintain per-requestor affinity for up to 5 minutes after a fallback; affinity decays with an exponential backoff to avoid long-term split-brain.
6) Observability and control: every fallback emits an event with reason, latency/cost delta, and pre/post model versions. Console exposes a per-pin degradation tolerance (percentage of requests allowed to degrade) and a manual override flow for Ops.

Trade-offs discussed:
- Safety vs Availability: Hard Pins are safest for correctness but can lead to increased errors during outages. Soft Pins improve availability but risk subtle semantic changes. We propose Soft Pin default because most customers prefer availability; however account policy can enforce Hard Pin.
- Complexity in resolver: adding token-buckets and cohort-preserving heuristics increases runtime complexity and memory. We will prototype with a capped in-memory cache and fall back to approximate counting when necessary.
- Cross-region fallbacks can introduce increased latency and data residency concerns. Default policy avoids cross-region fallback for accounts with residency restrictions; Console warns when enabling cross-region fallback.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Spike (1 week): bench a lightweight in-memory token-bucket implementation and simulate capacity bursts with pinned traffic mixes. Link: https://drive.redwood.com/spikes/eng/region-pin-token-bucket (design notes).
- Spec PR (this ticket) -> review with PM/Product and Security.
- Prototype in staging (2 sprints): runtime resolver changes behind a feature flag + rollout controller changes to tag canary cohorts. Create a synthetic test harness that replays production traces with pinned variants.
- Console UI (parallel): read-only timeline + degradation tolerance toggle behind feature flag. Mock link: https://drive.redwood.com/designs/console-pin-degrade-v1.
- E2E tests and runbook updates -> beta with select customers -> full launch.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Default pin mode: Soft or Hard? (PM leaning: Soft by default with explicit Hard opt-in).
- Sticky affinity TTL (proposal 5 minutes) — ops and client SDK feedback required.
- How to present audit logs for compliance customers without flooding logs? (proposal: roll up events and provide sampling + on-demand expanded logs).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Incorrect fallback leads to data residency violation. Mitigation: block cross-region fallback for accounts with residency flags; raise Alert on any cross-region fallbacks.
- Risk: Fallbacks skew canary metrics. Mitigation: cohort-preserving heuristics and labeling of fallback events so evals can filter them out.

comments: 2026-02-19 - Tomás Nguyen: Ran initial token-bucket microbench locally. Prototype shows <1% additional tail latency under 10k rps burst when short-circuiting fallback logic. Need to confirm memory overhead in long-lived resolvers.

2026-02-21 - Marta Kline (PM): PM prefers Soft Pin default to minimize customer errors; asked for explicit UI language and audit path for Hard Pin. Also requested a sample of customers who currently rely on pinning to estimate impact.

2026-02-25 - Security review (Ben Holt): Flagged cross-region fallback as a compliance blocker for accounts with residency controls. Agreed to add guardrails and an account-level boolean to disable cross-region fallback.
2026-03-03 - Design review (Lena Morrison): Provided Console mock feedback — suggested adding a timeline filter for 'fallback only' events and a quick link to open the raw audit row in Logs.
2026-03-08 - Tomás Nguyen: Created initial staging branch and feature flag. PR linked above. Running load replays now; next: add cohort-preserving checks and sticky affinity store.
2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Updated acceptance criteria to require an audit-sampling strategy for high-volume accounts to avoid log noise.
